doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Singing the 'Saved by the Bell' theme
summary: He sang and played bass on the theme at Bill Schnee's studio, with named musicians and network executives asking for changes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Do you ever hear things on television or on the radio that you played on?

Yeah. I hear maybe the most played thing that I hear is this theme from this TV show called “Saved by the Bell” which I ended up playing bass on and I also ended up singing the lead vocal and background vocals with a friend of mine, Sunny Wilkinson. So every now and then — it’s still being played on cable and it tickles me because we never expected, we didn’t know what this was going to be. I happened to know the guy that wrote the theme. He heard me sing at his company’s Christmas party. And that’s why I got the call to do it, through mutual friends. So I sang the demo for him and then maybe two or three months later he called me up and he said, “Hey man would you be into like we’re going to cut this thing and a few other cues for a pilot,” so we went out to Bill Schnee’s studio and I walk in and Rich Ames, his writing partner, a great keyboard player was playing keyboards. And let’s see, Jim Keltner is the drummer, one of my heroes, and so we just start running this and we did, I don’t know, maybe 35 cues and the main title. Oh and Dean Parks was playing guitar. So I thought wow, this is a fun date. And the tune was simple, it was fine and Keltner did his beautiful thing on it and everybody played great on it. And then Sunny and I hung around and I sang the theme again. And it was really funny because the NBC suits were behind the glass. So they’re getting on the talkback and they’re going, “Okay that’s great, that’s great. Can you make it a little more rock & roll?” So I go like okay. So I try to make it a little more rock & roll. “Well that was great, that was great. Could you enunciate a little more?” But so I just hung in there and they were cool and finally they went click — we got it. And next thing I knew it was on the air. And what was amazing about it is the show went from pilot to a regular show and then a spinoff called “Saved By The Bell, The New Class” was created, which was also running, and they used the same theme. And Sunny Wilkinson, bless her heart, they wanted us to do a buyout, which is just a set fee.
Oh like you’re going to get paid for the date.
